title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
statement: Given a list sorted in non-decreasing order and a target, find the two positions whose values add up to the target. Return them as 1-based indices [i, j] with i < j. Exactly one pair exists.

hints.1_question: The array is sorted. How could looking at the smallest and largest value together tell you which one to change?
hints.2_nudge: Put one pointer at each end. If the sum is too small, which pointer should move? If too big?
hints.3_big_hint: While l < r: s = a[l] + a[r]. If s == target return [l+1, r+1]; if s < target l += 1; else r -= 1.

known_bugs.name: returns 0-based indices
known_bugs.followup: Re-read the output format. Are indices counted from 0 or from 1?

known_bugs.name: moves pointers the wrong way
known_bugs.followup: If the sum is too small, would moving the right pointer left make it bigger or smaller?

known_bugs.name: assumes values are positive
known_bugs.followup: Is it always true that a number bigger than the target can't be part of the answer? What if values can be negative?

followups: What would you do if the array were not sorted?
Why doesn't this approach miss a valid pair when it moves a pointer?
